one_line: Pallava commander of Narasimhavarman I and Shaiva devotee remembered as the Nayanar Siruthondar.

appearance.age_look: early 40s, athletic and broad-shouldered, seasoned warrior’s build
appearance.face: oval face, medium brown South Indian complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed moustache, a small horizontal vibhuti mark across the forehead, calm serious eyes with a resolute yet compassionate default expression
appearance.hair: thick black hair pulled back into a high, modest warrior’s kudumi (topknot) at the rear crown, sides neatly smoothed, no shaved areas; simple narrow gold circlet resting above the forehead, leaving the vibhuti visible
appearance.costume: Pallava-period South Indian warrior dress: a knee-length deep maroon cotton tunic with short sleeves and a slightly flared hem, worn over a cream-colored dhoti wrapped tightly at the waist and pleated to fall just above the ankles; a broad dark brown leather war-belt securing the dhoti with a simple bronze buckle; over the tunic, a sleeveless fitted vest of dull bronze scale-like metal plates (light lamellar armour) covering chest and upper torso without fantastical decoration; a long mustard-yellow angavastra shawl with a thin maroon border draped from left shoulder across the back and looping to the right forearm; simple leather bracers on both wrists, and plain dark brown leather sandals; minimal jewellery—small round gold stud earrings and a single sacred thread (yajnopavita) drawn diagonally across the chest, visible where the armour slightly parts near the shoulder.
appearance.signature: A long straight Pallava-style steel sword with a gently tapering single-edged blade, simple iron guard, and wooden hilt wrapped in dark brown leather, held sheathed in a plain brown scabbard at his left hip; in his right hand he often cradles a small, dark stone Ganapati idol with carved draped garments and a subtle sash, symbolizing the Vatapi Ganapati tradition.

ref_desc: Paranjothi Siruthondar is a medium-brown, mustached Pallava commander with a vibhuti-marked forehead, black hair in a high kudumi and gold circlet, wearing maroon tunic, cream dhoti, bronze vest, mustard angavastra, leather gear, and carrying a sheathed sword plus a small draped stone Ganapati idol.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Paranjothi Siruthondar, a dignified early-40s South Indian Pallava commander and Shaiva devotee: medium brown complexion, oval face, sharp nose, neat moustache, calm serious eyes, and a small horizontal vibhuti mark on his forehead. His thick black hair is pulled into a high kudumi topknot at the rear crown, sides smoothed, with a simple narrow gold circlet above the forehead that leaves the vibhuti visible. Dress him in historically grounded Pallava-period warrior clothing: a knee-length deep maroon cotton tunic with short sleeves over a tightly wrapped cream dhoti pleated to just above the ankles; a broad dark brown leather war-belt with a plain bronze buckle; and a sleeveless fitted vest of dull bronze scale-like metal plates covering his chest and upper torso as practical lamellar armour. Add a long mustard-yellow angavastra shawl with thin maroon border draped from his left shoulder across his back, looping to rest on his right forearm, simple leather bracers on both wrists, dark brown leather sandals, small round gold stud earrings, and a visible sacred thread crossing the chest at the shoulder opening of the armour. At his left hip hangs a plain brown scabbard holding a straight Pallava-style sword with a gently tapering single-edged blade, simple iron guard, and a wooden hilt wrapped in dark brown leather; in his right hand he gently cradles a small dark stone Ganapati idol depicted fully draped with carved garments and a sash. Use deep maroon, cream, mustard yellow, dark brown, and dull bronze as the dominant colours, and pose him in a steady, heroic stance that conveys both martial discipline and devotional calm.
